data.title: Cross-Platform Deposit and Withdrawal Chain
data.description: Detects a pattern where funds are received via one payment rail (e.g., ACH, wire) and then immediately sent out via a different payment rail (e.g., Zelle, FedNow) within a short window. This cross-rail chaining is a common layering technique used to obscure the origin of funds and complicate tracing, often associated with money mule operations and authorized push payment fraud monetization.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Cross-Platform Deposit and Withdrawal Chain")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: (selection_inbound and selection_outbound and filter_amount) | temporal(ordered=true, maxspan=4h, by=account_id)")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
event_type="payment_received"
(inbound_rail="ACH_IN" OR inbound_rail="WIRE_IN" OR inbound_rail="RTP_IN" OR inbound_rail="FEDNOW_IN")
event_type="instant_payment_initiated"
(outbound_rail="ZELLE" OR outbound_rail="FEDNOW" OR outbound_rail="RTP" OR outbound_rail="ACH_SAMEDAY")
outbound_amount_pct_of_inbound>=80
| transaction account_id maxspan=4h
| where eventcount >= 2

falsepositives: Freelancer receiving ACH payroll and immediately paying rent via Zelle
Business account receiving wire payment and disbursing to vendors via instant payment
